001: Ivan, have you found where to stay in Moscow yet?
Not yet, Maria. I looked at a couple of options, but I just can't seem to choose.
And which area suits you? Maybe I can suggest something.
I'd like to be closer to the center, so I don't spend a lot of time on the road.
Then look at an apartment on Patriarch's Ponds, it's very convenient there.
Thanks for the advice! I'll look at that option today.
002: Dmitry, have you booked a hotel room yet?
Not yet, Olga. I'm waiting for a response from one hotel.
Why is it taking so long? They usually reply within a day.
They're asking me to confirm the booking by phone, but I can't get through.
Try emailing them again, sometimes that works faster.
Good idea. I'll write to them right now.
003: Hello! I'd like to book a room for two nights.
Hello! What dates are you planning to check in?
From Friday to Sunday, if you have any rooms available.
Yes, we have a standard room available with breakfast.
Great, that works for me. How much will it cost?
The price will be six thousand rubles per night.
004: Sergey, have you decided where you'll stay during the conference?
I'm still deciding between a hotel and renting an apartment.
And what's the difference in price? I guess an apartment is more economical?
The apartment is cheaper, but you have to pay a deposit and wait for the owner.
Then maybe it's easier to take a hotel, so there's no extra hassle?
You're right, it's probably more reliable that way. I'll book a room today.
005: Hello, I booked a room with you online.
Good afternoon! Could you please give me your last name?
My last name is Sokolova, the booking is for today.
Yes, I see your booking. Room three hundred five, on the third floor.
Tell me, is breakfast included in the price?
Yes, breakfast is served from seven to ten in the morning.
006: Olga, I found a great place to stay, but it doesn't have a kitchen.
Do you really need a kitchen? You can eat at restaurants.
Yes, but I'm used to cooking myself, it's both cheaper and healthier.
Then look for an apartment with a kitchen, the websites have filters.
Right, I didn't think about filters. Thanks for the tip!
You're welcome. I hope you find what you need.
007: Dmitry, have you paid for the apartment booking yet?
Not yet, I'm waiting for the payment details from the owner.
And did you check the reviews for this place?
Yes, the reviews are good, but I'm still a little worried.
Maybe ask the owner to show you a video of the room?
Great idea! That way I can make sure everything is fine.
008: Hello, I'd like to extend my stay at the hotel.
Hello, for how many days would you like to extend?
For two more days, if that's possible.
Yes, of course. Your room is available, so there's no problem.
You're welcome, I'll arrange the extension right now.
009: Ivan, how do you like the hotel you booked?
Overall it's not bad, but the windows face a noisy street.
That's unpleasant. Did you try asking for a different room?
Yes, I spoke to the front desk, but there are no other rooms available.
That's a shame. And does the air conditioning in the room work well?
The air conditioning works great, so I don't have to open the windows.
010: Maria, have you booked accommodation for the weekend yet?
Yes, I rented an apartment not far from the park.
Sounds wonderful! And how did you find it?
A colleague recommended it to me, she stays there often.
It's convenient when you have a tried-and-true option.
I agree. The main thing is that everything is as good as she described.
